ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: It is known that the side length of square $ABCD$ is 4. Square $OMNE$ (with $OM > \frac{1}{2}AC$) rotates around the center of symmetry $O$ of square $ABCD$. What is the area of the overlapping region of the two squares?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, connect AC and BD. Let OE intersect CD at point Q, and OM intersect BC at point P,

$\because$ Point O is the center of the square ABCD,

$\therefore$ The diagonals of square ABCD intersect at point O,

$\therefore \angle$ODQ=$\angle$OCP=$45^\circ$, OD=OC, $\angle$COD=$90^\circ$,

$\because$ Quadrilateral OMNE is a square,

$\therefore \angle$EOM=$90^\circ$,

$\because \angle$DOC=$\angle$DOQ+$\angle$COQ=$90^\circ$, $\angle$EOM=$\angle$COQ+$\angle$COP=$90^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle$DOQ=$\angle$COP,

In $\triangle DOE$ and $\triangle AOF$,

$\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \angle DOQ=\angle COP \\ OD=OC \\ \angle ODQ=\angle OCP \end{array} \right.$,

$\therefore \triangle DOQ \cong \triangle COP$ (ASA),

$\therefore S_{\triangle DOQ}=S_{\triangle COP}$,

$\therefore$ The area of quadrilateral OPCQ=$S_{\triangle OCP}+S_{\triangle QOC}=S_{\triangle ODQ}+S_{\triangle QOC}=S_{\triangle COD}$,

$\because S_{\triangle COD}=\frac{1}{4}S_{\text{square ABCD}}=\frac{1}{4}\times 4\times 4=4$,

$\therefore$ The area of the overlapping part of the two squares is $\boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is square ABCD, A and B are on the left side, D and C are on the right side, and O is the center of square ABCD; on the right side there is square OMNE rotated around O, side OE extends from O toward the upper right, and side OM extends from O toward the lower right. Thus △ODQ and △OCP have two angles and the included side correspondingly equal, namely ∠ODQ = ∠OCP, OD = OC, ∠DOQ = ∠COP, therefore △ODQ ≅ △OCP, and their areas are equal. The area of overlapping quadrilateral OPCQ is S△OCP + S△OQC; replacing with congruent triangles gives S△ODQ + S△OQC = S△ODC. △ODC is one of the four equal-area triangles into which square ABCD is divided by its diagonals, so its area is (1/4)×4² = 4.

method.method_draft: Use the intersection-point and triangle-congruence route. From the diagram, take the shaded overlap as quadrilateral OPCQ, where ray OE of the rotating square meets side CD of square ABCD at Q, and ray OM meets side BC at P. Connect OC and OD. Since O is the center of square ABCD, OC = OD, angle COD = 90°, and the diagonals make 45° with the sides, so angle ODQ = angle OCP = 45°. Since OMNE is a square, OE ⟂ OM, so angle EOM = 90°. Comparing the decompositions of the two right angles around O gives angle DOQ = angle COP. Therefore triangles ODQ and OCP are congruent by ASA. Hence their areas are equal. Replace triangle OCP in the overlap quadrilateral OPCQ by congruent triangle ODQ: area(OPCQ) = area(OQC) + area(OCP) = area(OQC) + area(ODQ) = area(ODC). Triangle ODC is one of four equal triangles formed by the diagonals of square ABCD, so its area is 1/4 · 4² = 4.

method.method_draft: Use a global symmetry-sector argument. From the diagram, regard the overlap as the part of square ABCD lying inside the right-angle wedge formed by the two adjacent rays OM and OE of square OMNE. Let L = OM. The text condition L > AC/2 means L is larger than the maximum distance from O to any point of ABCD, since AC/2 is the circumradius of square ABCD. Therefore the far sides MN and EN of square OMNE cannot cut off any part of ABCD inside that wedge; the overlap equals ABCD intersected with the infinite 90° sector between OM and OE. Now extend the two perpendicular lines through O containing OM and OE. They divide the plane into four 90° sectors. Because ABCD is a square centered at O, a 90° rotation about O maps ABCD to itself and maps each sector to the next sector. Thus the four sector-intersections with ABCD have equal area. raw_record.original_question: It is known that the side length of square $ABCD$ is 4. Square $OMNE$ (with $OM > \frac{1}{2}AC$) rotates around the center of symmetry $O$ of square $ABCD$. What is the area of the overlapping region of the two squares?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, connect AC and BD. Let OE intersect CD at point Q, and OM intersect BC at point P,

$\because$ Point O is the center of the square ABCD,

$\therefore$ The diagonals of square ABCD intersect at point O,

$\therefore \angle$ODQ=$\angle$OCP=$45^\circ$, OD=OC, $\angle$COD=$90^\circ$,

$\because$ Quadrilateral OMNE is a square,

$\therefore \angle$EOM=$90^\circ$,

$\because \angle$DOC=$\angle$DOQ+$\angle$COQ=$90^\circ$, $\angle$EOM=$\angle$COQ+$\angle$COP=$90^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle$DOQ=$\angle$COP,

In $\triangle DOE$ and $\triangle AOF$,

$\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \angle DOQ=\angle COP \\ OD=OC \\ \angle ODQ=\angle OCP \end{array} \right.$,

$\therefore \triangle DOQ \cong \triangle COP$ (ASA),

$\therefore S_{\triangle DOQ}=S_{\triangle COP}$,

$\therefore$ The area of quadrilateral OPCQ=$S_{\triangle OCP}+S_{\triangle QOC}=S_{\triangle ODQ}+S_{\triangle QOC}=S_{\triangle COD}$,

$\because S_{\triangle COD}=\frac{1}{4}S_{\text{square ABCD}}=\frac{1}{4}\times 4\times 4=4$,

$\therefore$ The area of the overlapping part of the two squares is $\boxed{4}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is square ABCD, A and B are on the left side, D and C are on the right side, and O is the center of square ABCD; on the right side there is square OMNE rotated around O, side OE extends from O toward the upper right, and side OM extends from O toward the lower right. The shaded overlapping part can be regarded as quadrilateral OPCQ, where Q is the intersection point of ray OE and side CD, and P is the intersection point of ray OM and side BC. Reasoning: Connect OC and OD. Because O is the center of square ABCD, OC = OD, and ∠COD = 90°. The diagonal of a square makes 45° with its side, therefore ∠ODQ = ∠OCP = 45°. Also because OMNE is a square, OE ⟂ OM, that is, ∠EOM = 90°. Near point O, ∠DOC = ∠DOQ + ∠QOC = 90°, while ∠EOM = ∠QOC + ∠COP = 90°, so ∠DOQ = ∠COP. Thus △ODQ and △OCP have two angles and the included side correspondingly equal, namely ∠ODQ = ∠OCP, OD = OC, ∠DOQ = ∠COP, therefore △ODQ ≅ △OCP, and their areas are equal. The area of overlapping quadrilateral OPCQ is S△OCP + S△OQC; replacing with congruent triangles gives S△ODQ + S△OQC = S△ODC. △ODC is one of the four equal-area triangles into which square ABCD is divided by its diagonals, so its area is (1/4)×4² = 4.
